body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 8233cacbf846adc3efa95315d7b9b61e6e94fb52 -->

Ready for the maintainer to merge.

What looks good:
- The rule covers each point of issue #4042: what a side branch is, the maintainer-only permit, the one-issue draft sub-PR with `--base side/<name>`, `Refs #N`, the sync rule (merge, never rebase, never force-push, after each related batch and at least each week), the local gates, the lane-count rule, and the switch-over that needs the maintainer's word.
- The two skills are changed only where a step would be wrong without the rule (one or two lines each). The decision file records what was decided, the dropped options and the cost to change later, in the format of `docs/decisions/README.md`.
- `Process change: yes` is present. `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is untouched. The body ends with `Fixes #4042`. `Changelog: none` is right for a docs-only PR.
- The trial merge against `origin/main` (267ee5096bde18de7c82f18bc93c041a773baa97) is clean. `gh pr view --json mergeable` reads MERGEABLE.

Results: docs and process files only, no code. No build, no tests and no gate were run, as the issue expects. This is not a build verdict. The only pre-check in the thread is the coordinator's read-only quick pass on the same head.

Targeted tests: none needed. The diff touches no post, no toolpath and no code path.

Requested before merge: none.

Questions / notes (not blocking):
1. The rule says a sub-PR merges when its review is clean, also as a `feat` (AGENTS.md, **Side branch**, the bullet starting "A sub-PR gets the quick pass"), but "When PRs merge" still reads "A `feat` or breaking PR merges at the minor/major cut" (AGENTS.md, **When PRs merge**). The intent - that the feat-at-cut rule applies to the switch-over PR, not to sub-PRs - is in docs/decisions/4042-side-branch-rule.md and the PR body, but it is not written where the two rules meet. One clause in the rule would close the gap, for example "The feat-at-cut rule applies to the switch-over."
2. The skills hard-code `side/path-kernel` (.claude/skills/work-issue/SKILL.md:38 and 120-122; .claude/skills/merge-ready/SKILL.md, the switch-over bullet) rather than the generic `side/<name>` of the rule. The rule is generic and says only `side/path-kernel` exists. A second side branch (maintainer-permitted) would make these lines wrong until edited. A `side/<name>` form with the path-kernel example kept would generalise the skills.

Notes on ASD-STE100 (not blocking): the rule text and the decision file use short sentences and one meaning per word; the phrase "as each other PR" (AGENTS.md, the "A sub-PR gets the quick pass" bullet) reads as "like any other PR" but is not a standard phrase in this repo. Optional: "as each other PR" -> "as any other PR".

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
